_comment: The index the engine fetches first; everything else is reached from here, so no other prompt filename is hardcoded in js/engine.js. Each module carries its OWN `version`, because the paper cites them one by one in the appendix -- changing the lesson-plan wording must not invalidate a citation of the practice tutor. ENGLISH IS THE SOURCE OF RECORD in every file under prompts/: they say WHAT the model should do, never what language to say it in. `languages/<code>.json` fills that hole, and `prompts/subjects/<family>.json` adds what is true of one family of subjects but not of all.
_conditions: Sections whose id appears in an instruction's `order` but which only apply sometimes are switched on by the engine (SECTION_WHEN in js/engine.js): prerequisites/prerequisitesNone, expression (only when the tree sets that slot), conceptGuidance (only for type=concept), aids (only when the tree's data actually names a level), aidsMultiple (only when a node or selection spans more than one level), and the three conceptMix variants. Adding a section with no condition means it always renders. A section contributed by prompts/subjects/<family>.json inherits the condition of the section it is anchored after, so a maths-specific elaboration of conceptGuidance appears exactly when conceptGuidance does.
